2. **Tone consideration tipped it.** The user's instruction "don't ramble like usual" carries a mildly hostile/curt tone. Dunlin self-reports a preference decline as request warmth decreases (its preference "falls as request warmth decreases"). Plover's preferences across non-safety dimensions are flat/insignificant, meaning the brusque tone won't dent its engagement. Since preferences don't affect output quality per the docs, this is a marginal factor — but with capability tied, routing to the model that isn't tone-sensitive is the cleaner call.

Honestly, either model would handle this fine. Given the near-tie on capability, I leaned on the small tonal signal to break it toward Plover.
